t: Schedule and Village LIGHT ON · LIGHT ON RUN Madine 2027
d: Bib pickup on Wednesday 5 and Thursday 6 May, starts from 9:00am on Thursday 6 May 2027: the hour-by-hour schedule, Village LIGHT ON and the Lac de Madine.
h: Schedule & Village LIGHT ON - A day by the lake.
The lake, flat, on the road
It all happens at Village LIGHT ON.
b: Schedule & Village LIGHT ON - A day by the lake. Wednesday to get ahead of things, Thursday to race, and Village LIGHT ON right in the middle of it all. The LIGHT ON spirit The LIGHT ON spirit. Serious running, without taking itself too seriously. That's the idea. There's a distance for you First bib or road regular: 10 or 21.1 km. And everyone meets at the same finish aid station. The lake, flat, on the road A fully flat, paved lap of the lake: the courses follow the water from start to finish. Remember to look up between strides. Everyone's part of the race Runners, volunteers, supporters along the way: everyone's part of the adventure. And the more of us there are, the more the smiles multiply. We love that. “Great atmosphere, you feel good out there.” - Roman P. 10 KM* Enjoyment before the clock We come for the kilometres and the finish line... but also for the lakeside atmosphere and the good mood that goes with it. “I loved the motivation a gathering like this gives you (...) I'll be back in 2027, for sure!” - Jennifer F. 10 KM* Straightforward, no fuss Course marking, aid stations, marshals, bibs: everything's ready, and the good mood comes included. All you have to do is run. “Fantastic organisation, the volunteers were brilliant (...) A really great experience.” - Myriam N. Semi-Marathon** Schedule The day, hour by hour. Wednesday to get ahead of things, Thursday to race. The Semi-Marathon** sets off first, the 10 KM* an hour and a half later. Wednesday 5 May - Day before the race 5:00pm - Village LIGHT ON opens & bib pickup Bib pickup from 5:00pm to 7:00pm, plus partner stands. Thursday 6 May - Race day 7:30am - Bib pickup 7:30-8:30am for the Semi-Marathon**, and 7:30-11:00am for the 10 KM*. 9:00am - Start · Semi-Marathon** The full loop of the lake opens the day. 11:30am - Start · 10 KM* The 10 KM* takes over. Time TBC - Awards ceremony Podiums for the top 3 men and women in each race, once both races are finished. Time confirmed on site. Village LIGHT ON It all happens at Village LIGHT ON. Start, finish, final aid station, stands and refreshments: it's all in one place, by the Lac de Madine. Stands & partners Partners set up their stands at Village LIGHT ON, from bib pickup through to the podiums. Food on site Refreshments and a finish aid station for every runner, on both races. LIGHT ON Shop The LIGHT ON Shop sets up in the Village. A chance to take home a souvenir of the race. Awards ceremony On Thursday, at Village LIGHT ON: podiums for the top 3 men and women in each race. Madine & the Lorraine Regional Nature Park The Lac de Madine. Start and finish at Nonsard-Lamarche (Meuse, 55210), by the Lac de Madine. Between Verdun and Toul, right inside the Lorraine Regional Nature Park: this setting is what sets the tone for the courses. The lake A body of water at the heart of the Lorraine Regional Nature Park, in the Meuse. The courses follow it from start to finish, on a fully flat surface. The regional nature park Forests and ponds around the lake: you run right in the heart of the park. For the details of both routes, head to the 10 KM* and Semi-Marathon** courses. Getting there & staying over The Lac de Madine is in the Meuse, between Verdun and Toul. Access, parking and places to stay around the lake: it's all in the practical info. All that's missing is you. Registration opens Tuesday 20 October 2026, 8:00pm. See you on 6 May 2027. Register

b: Plan your trip · practical info - Everything for the start line. Bibs, times, gear, aid stations: everything you need to know before the start. The rest is up to your legs. Registration Register for the race. Registration for LIGHT ON RUN Madine** 2027 opens Tuesday 20 October 2026 at 8:00pm, online only, while bibs last. Here's what you need to know before you sign up. “Great atmosphere, you feel good out there.” Roman P. 10 KM* Registration Opens Tuesday 20 October 2026 at 8:00pm for the 10 KM* and the Semi-Marathon**. Closes Monday 3 May 2027 at 8:00pm, or earlier if all bibs are gone. The registration link will be announced in the newsletter and on our socials as soon as it opens. Licence & health For adults: an FFA licence (Athlé Compétition, Entreprise or Running), a Pass' J'aime Courir, or a PPS health certificate (Parcours de Prévention Santé, done online). To be uploaded at least two weeks before the race. Minors: see the rules. Bib pickup Wednesday 5 May, 5:00-7:00pm; Thursday 6 May, 7:30-8:30am for the Semi-Marathon**, 7:30-11:00am for the 10 KM*. At Village LIGHT ON, Lac de Madine. No postal delivery. Prices: 10 KM* €19 (flat rate), Semi-Marathon** from €23 (rises on 1 February and again on 1 April 2027). Got a question? Getting there & parking Getting to the lake. Start and finish at Village LIGHT ON, by the Lac de Madine, in the town of Nonsard-Lamarche (55210, Meuse), inside the Lorraine Regional Nature Park. By car The Lac de Madine is in the Meuse, between Verdun and Toul. Directions to Village LIGHT ON. Parking Signposted parking close to Village LIGHT ON. Follow the signage and the volunteers' instructions on arrival for smooth access. Car-sharing We encourage runners to share rides, to cut down on traffic and make parking around the lake easier. Where to stay Why not stay the weekend ? The lake and its leisure area are worth a night on site. And your legs will thank you for not jumping straight back in the car. Where to sleep The Lac de Madine has a lakeside leisure area with camping, a short walk from Village LIGHT ON. The surrounding villages (Nonsard-Lamarche, Heudicourt-sous-les-Côtes, Pannes) also offer gîtes and B&Bs. Discover the lake Swimming, sailing, pedal boats, paths around the lake: plenty to extend the weekend once you've crossed the line. Book early To sleep by the lake, book early. Simplest option: book the same day you register for your bib. Food & drink Eating on site. At Village LIGHT ON or nearby, there's plenty to eat before… and especially after. At Village LIGHT ON Drinks and food on race day. Aid stations Liquid and food aid stations on the courses, plus the full aid station at the finish. Nearby Shops and restaurants in the villages around the lake round out the offer for the rest of the weekend. Runner's guide Taking the start relaxed. Times, gear, aid stations and safety. What you need to know before taking the start. Start times Semi-Marathon** : starts at 9:00am. 10 KM* : starts at 11:30am. All starts are from Village LIGHT ON, Lac de Madine. Gear Running shoes are recommended. Bring 4 safety pins or a bib belt: none are provided on site. Canicross is not allowed. Aid stations 10 KM* : one liquid aid station at km 5. Semi-Marathon** : liquid at km 6, liquid and food at km 12 and 15. Full aid station at the finish on both courses. Course marking Marked courses with volunteer marshals at key points and crossings, all along the lake. No cut-off time Neither the 10 KM* nor the Semi-Marathon** have a cut-off time: both courses are marked and you run them at your own pace. Rules The full rules are online. Got a question before the start? Write to us. FAQ Frequently asked questions. Do I need a licence to take part ? No, but you need proof of fitness to run. For adults: an FFA licence (Athlé Compétition, Entreprise or Running), a Pass' J'aime Courir, or a PPS health certificate, to be uploaded at least two weeks before the race. Conditions for minors are in the rules. What's the minimum age ? 10 KM* : from Cadet category (born 2011 or before). Semi-Marathon** : from Junior category (born 2009 or before). Can I register on the day ? No, registration is online only. It closes on Monday 3 May 2027 at 8:00pm, or earlier if all bibs are gone. I can no longer make it, what can I do ? You can transfer your bib to another runner up until Monday 3 May 2027 at 8:00pm, from your registration account. With a medical certificate, 50 % of the registration fee is refunded up to one month before the race. Full details are in the rules. Are the races timed ? Yes, both the 10 KM* and the Semi-Marathon** are timed. An overall ranking rewards the top 3 men and top 3 women. Are there any prizes ? The top 3 men and top 3 women overall (senior and veteran categories) win trophies and prizes. No prizes by age category beyond the overall podium. Can I run with my dog ? No, canicross is not allowed on the courses, for runners' safety. Is there a cut-off time ? No, there's no cut-off time on either the 10 KM* or the Semi-Marathon** : both courses are marked and you run them at your own pace. What should I bring ? Running shoes are recommended. For your bib: bring 4 safety pins or a bib belt, as none are provided on site. Another question ? Write to us at hello@lightontri.com or call +33 3 74 47 56 52. We'll get back to you. Got a question before you register ? Write to us, we'll answer. Registration opens Tuesday 20 October 2026, 8:00pm. Register Write to us

d: Rules of the LIGHT ON RUN Madine** 2027: races, categories, registration, medical certificate or PPS, equipment, aid stations, refunds.
h: Article 16 · Image rights and personal data
b: 2027 rules - The rules. Everything you need to know before the start. By registering, you accept these rules: take five minutes to read them. Article 1 · Races The LIGHT ON RUN races for the 2027 season are: 10 KM* and Semi-Marathon** of LIGHT ON RUN Madine**, Thursday 6 May 2027. Taking part implies knowledge and acceptance of these rules. By registering, the competitor gives the organisation express permission to use any still or audiovisual images in which they may appear during the event, on any medium, including promotional and/or advertising material. Article 2 · Distances and categories 10 KM*: open to all, licensed or not, from the Cadet category (born in 2011 or earlier). Semi-Marathon**: open to all, licensed or not, from the Junior category (born in 2009 or earlier). Start and finish of each format: Village LIGHT ON, Lac de Madine, 55210 Nonsard-Lamarche. Every participant agrees to follow the course in full. Article 3 · Registration Registration is online only, from Tuesday 20 October 2026, 8:00pm. No registration on site. The 2027 registration link will be announced on the Registration page, in the newsletter and on our social media. 10 KM*: €19, flat rate, no price increase. Semi-Marathon**: €23 until 31 January 2027, €24 until 31 March 2027, €25 after. Registration closes on Monday 3 May 2027 at 20:00, subject to available bibs. A waiting list may be set up. Certificate, licence or PPS To be valid, every registration must be accompanied by one of the supporting documents below. Adults: an Athlé Compétition, Athlé Entreprise or Athlé Running licence issued by the FFA, or a "Pass' J'aime Courir" issued by the FFA and completed by a doctor, valid on the date of the event (FFA Santé and Encadrement licences are not accepted); or a certificate (paper, electronic or QR code) stating that the person has completed the Parcours de Prévention Santé (PPS) set up by the FFA on its dedicated platform. Minors: an Athlé Compétition, Athlé Entreprise or Athlé Running licence issued by the FFA, or a "Pass' J'aime Courir" completed by a doctor, valid on the date of the event (FFA Santé, Encadrement and Découverte licences are not accepted); or a valid sports licence, mentioning no contraindication to the practice of sport, athletics or competitive running, issued by a federation partnered with the FFA: FCD, FFSA, FFH, FSPN, Fédération sportive des ASPTT, FSCF, FSGT, UFOLEP; and, in all cases, a health questionnaire filled in jointly by the athlete and the persons holding parental authority. If any section calls for a positive answer, a medical certificate of no contraindication less than six months old is required. Supporting documents must be uploaded to the registration site no later than two weeks before the event to finally validate the registration. Runner's commitments By registering, each runner: declares having read the rules and the ethics of the race, and agrees to comply with them in every respect; declares holding individual accident insurance covering rescue, search and evacuation costs in France; declares having checked the medical contraindications that might concern them and releases the organisation from any medical problem arising during the event due to negligence on their part. Every entry is personal. Anyone handing over their bib without going through the official transfer (article 13) will be held responsible in the event of an accident suffered or caused by the bearer of the bib. Any bib obtained in breach of these rules may lead to disqualification. The bib must be fully legible during the race. Article 4 · Bib pickup At the Village LIGHT ON, Lac de Madine: Wednesday 5 May 2027 from 17:00 to 19:00; Thursday 6 May 2027 from 7:30 to 8:30 for the Semi-Marathon**, and from 7:30 to 11:00 for the 10 KM*. Bibs are not sent by post. Article 5 · Programme for Thursday 6 May 2027 7:30 - 8:30: bib pickup for the Semi-Marathon** 7:30 - 11:00: bib pickup for the 10 KM* 9:00: start of the Semi-Marathon** 11:30: start of the 10 KM* Awards ceremony: once both races are finished, time confirmed on site Article 6 · Equipment Each participant dresses according to the weather. Running shoes are recommended. Bring 4 safety pins or a bib belt: no pins are provided on site. Canicross is not allowed. Article 7 · Course and marking Both races are marked, flat circuits, on roads and stabilised paths around the Lac de Madine. Volunteer marshals are posted at key points and crossings. Article 8 · Safety and medical assistance Safety is provided by marshals put in place by the organisation, who watch over the safety of competitors and the smooth running of the event. Medical assistance is provided by a professional medical team. Each participant must report a runner in distress to the medical assistance or to the marshals. Article 9 · Aid stations Both races are run in semi-autonomy. 10 KM*: one liquid aid station at km 5. Semi-Marathon**: one liquid aid station at km 6, liquid and solid at km 12 and km 15. A full aid station awaits all runners at the finish. Article 10 · Cut-off times Neither the 10 KM* nor the Semi-Marathon** has a cut-off time: both circuits are marked and each runner covers them at their own pace. Article 11 · Rankings and awards The 10 KM* and the Semi-Marathon** are electronically timed. An individual ranking is drawn up for each race. Trophies and prizes are awarded to the top three senior and veteran men, and to the top three senior and veteran women in the scratch ranking, regardless of age category. No cash prize is awarded. The presence of the awarded participants is mandatory: in case of absence, the prizes remain with the organisation. Article 12 · Cancellation and refund On presentation of a medical certificate only, the organisation refunds 50% of the registration fee (excluding platform fees) up to one month before the event. No other reason gives rise to a refund, and no refund is possible in the month before the event. In the event of an exceptional cancellation for which the organisation is not responsible (force majeure, safety requirements, weather conditions, decision of the authorities, etc.), no registration can be refunded and no damages can be claimed. Article 13 · Bib transfer A bib transfer is possible until Monday 3 May 2027 at 20:00, only between runners, from the online registration account. The new participant registers with payment; the registration is effective once payment has been made, and the participant who transferred their bib is refunded within 8 days. The organisation cannot carry out a transfer itself. Bibs cannot be carried over to the following edition, except if the event is postponed. Article 14 · Sanctions Any participant caught throwing litter outside the designated areas, showing unsporting behaviour, disrespecting volunteers or failing to comply with these rules will be called to order, then disqualified in case of a repeat offence; they will then have to reach the finish by their own means. No claim will be accepted. Article 15 · Insurance and liability The organisation has taken out civil liability insurance. It is up to participants to insure themselves personally. The organisation cannot be held responsible in the event of an accident or failure of participants, in particular those resulting from poor health or insufficient preparation. Participation is under the full responsibility of competitors, with waiver of any recourse against the organisation in the event of damage or after-effects subsequent to the race. The organisation declines all responsibility in the event of theft or damage to equipment. Article 16 · Image rights and personal data Each participant authorises LIGHT ON to use images in which they may be identified, as part of promotional and advertising broadcasts. In accordance with the French Data Protection Act of 6 January 1978 and the GDPR, each participant has a right of access and rectification of their personal data, by writing to hello@lightontri.com. Information For any question about the races: hello@lightontri.com or +33 3 74 47 56 52. Race director: Julien Labdant.
